newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar off highs but well supported in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Dollar off highs but well supported in Singapore.

text.p: The dollar lost its footing against the yen on Wednesday as comments by a U.S. official stirred renewed concern about Japan's current account surplus with the United States, Singapore dealers said.

Lawrence Greenwood, economic minister-counsellor at the U.S. embassy in Tokyo, told Reuters Financial Television rises in Japan's current account surplus had potential to create an explosive situation with the United States.
His comments pushed the dollar down to the brink of 119 yen but dealers said it would be supported at that level with falls expected to be limited to 118.80 yen at worst.
"Dollar/yen broke the 119 level which is supposed to be bullish. But it came off because of this statement about U.S. trade problems," a European bank dealer said.
He said the dollar's gains were expected to be capped above 119.60 yen for the time being.
He said the dollar's rise against the mark was being blocked partly by talk of offers from a European airplane manufacturer around the 1.8820/30 mark level.
"I don't believe the rumour though. It will eventually go through," he said.
He added that the dollar looked well bid around 1.8780 marks and any pullback was likely to be limited to short-term profit taking.
"It's like a one-way ticket. Those hedge funds who've been buying haven't taken profit yet. They're looking at 1.90 marks," he said.
